subproblems.title: Coordinate Steiner symmetrization: reflection symmetries
subproblems.statement: Let d ∈ ℕ, j ∈ Fin d and let A ⊆ ℝ^d = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) be arbitrary. For y ∈ ℝ^d, i ∈ Fin d and t ∈ ℝ let y[i↦t] be y with its i-th coordinate replaced by t (Lean: WithLp.toLp 2 (Function.update y.ofLp i t)), R_i(y) := y[i↦−y_i] (reflection in the coordinate hyperplane x_i = 0), A^j_y := {t ∈ ℝ : y[j↦t] ∈ A}, λ(y) := (L¹(A^j_y)).toReal (L¹ = Lebesgue measure on ℝ), and S_j(A) := {y ∈ ℝ^d : A^j_y ≠ ∅ and |y_j| ≤ λ(y)/2}. Then (a) R_j(y) ∈ S_j(A) for every y ∈ S_j(A); and (b) for every i ∈ Fin d with i ≠ j: if R_i(x) ∈ A for all x ∈ A, then R_i(y) ∈ S_j(A) for all y ∈ S_j(A).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (d : ℕ) (j : Fin d) (A : Set (Euclid d)), (∀ x ∈ {y : Euclid d | {t : ℝ | WithLp.toLp 2 (Function.update y.ofLp j t) ∈ A}.Nonempty ∧ |y j| ≤ (volume {t : ℝ | WithLp.toLp 2 (Function.update y.ofLp j t) ∈ A}).toReal / 2}, WithLp.toLp 2 (Function.update x.ofLp j (-x j)) ∈ {y : Euclid d | {t : ℝ | WithLp.toLp 2 (Function.update y.ofLp j t) ∈ A}.Nonempty ∧ |y j| ≤ (volume {t : ℝ | WithLp.toLp 2 (Function.update y.ofLp j t) ∈ A}).toReal / 2}) ∧ ∀ i : Fin d, i ≠ j → (∀ x ∈ A, WithLp.toLp 2 (Function.update x.ofLp i (-x i)) ∈ A) → ∀ x ∈ {y : Euclid d | {t : ℝ | WithLp.toLp 2 (Function.update y.ofLp j t) ∈ A}.Nonempty ∧ |y j| ≤ (volume {t : ℝ | WithLp.toLp 2 (Function.update y.ofLp j t) ∈ A}).toReal / 2}, WithLp.toLp 2 (Function.update x.ofLp i (-x i)) ∈ {y : Euclid d | {t : ℝ | WithLp.toLp 2 (Function.update y.ofLp j t) ∈ A}.Nonempty ∧ |y j| ≤ (volume {t : ℝ | WithLp.toLp 2 (Function.update y.ofLp j t) ∈ A}).toReal / 2}
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent step 1f (Simon, Ch. 1, proof of 2.10, book/chapter-01.txt lines 525–527: if i ≠ j and A is invariant under reflection in the i-th coordinate plane, then S_j(A) is invariant under reflection in both the i-th and the j-th coordinate planes). Notation as in the statement; y_i is y.ofLp i (written y i in Lean) and (WithLp.toLp 2 f)_i = f i (PiLp.toLp_apply, simp). For y ∈ ℝ^d the point ξ := y[j↦0] lies in H_j = {x_j = 0}, A^j_y is the parent's A_ξ, and y ∈ S_j(A) iff A_ξ ≠ ∅ and |y_j| ≤ λ(ξ)/2, so S_j(A) is the parent's set of step 1b. No compactness or measurability is used.
1. Coordinate rules. For z ∈ ℝ^d, indices i, k and reals s, t: (z[i↦t])_i = t; (z[i↦t])_k = z_k for k ≠ i (Function.update_self, Function.update_of_ne); (z[i↦s])[i↦t] = z[i↦t] (Function.update_idem). Two points of ℝ^d are equal iff all their coordinates agree (ext).
2. Proof of (a). Let y ∈ S_j(A) and y' := R_j(y) = y[j↦−y_j]. By step 1, y'[j↦t] = y[j↦t] for every t ∈ ℝ, so A^j_{y'} = A^j_y and λ(y') = λ(y). Also y'_j = −y_j, so |y'_j| = |y_j|. Hence A^j_{y'} = A^j_y ≠ ∅ and |y'_j| = |y_j| ≤ λ(y)/2 = λ(y')/2, i.e. R_j(y) ∈ S_j(A).
3. Proof of (b): commutation. Fix i ≠ j such that R_i(x) ∈ A for all x ∈ A. Let y ∈ S_j(A) and y' := R_i(y) = y[i↦−y_i]. For every t ∈ ℝ, y'[j↦t] = R_i(y[j↦t]). Compare k-th coordinates: for k = j both sides equal t (R_i leaves coordinate j ≠ i unchanged, and (y[j↦t])_j = t); for k = i the left side is y'_i = −y_i and the right side is −(y[j↦t])_i = −y_i because i ≠ j; for k ∉ {i, j} both sides equal y_k.
4. R_i is an involution: R_i(R_i(z)) = z for every z ∈ ℝ^d (coordinate i: −(−z_i) = z_i; all other coordinates are unchanged).
5. Equal slices. A^j_{y'} = A^j_y. If t ∈ A^j_{y'}, then R_i(y[j↦t]) = y'[j↦t] ∈ A by step 3, so by the invariance of A and step 4, y[j↦t] = R_i(R_i(y[j↦t])) ∈ A, i.e. t ∈ A^j_y. Conversely, if y[j↦t] ∈ A, then y'[j↦t] = R_i(y[j↦t]) ∈ A by invariance. Consequently λ(y') = λ(y).
6. Conclusion of (b). Since i ≠ j, y'_j = y_j. Therefore A^j_{y'} = A^j_y ≠ ∅ and |y'_j| = |y_j| ≤ λ(y)/2 = λ(y')/2, i.e. R_i(y) ∈ S_j(A). ∎
proof_key_steps: Coordinate rules for y[i↦t]: update_self, update_of_ne, update_idem; points are equal iff coordinates agree.
(a) R_j(y)[j↦t] = y[j↦t], so the j-slice and λ are unchanged, and |(R_j y)_j| = |y_j|.
(b) For i ≠ j: R_i(y)[j↦t] = R_i(y[j↦t]) and R_i is an involution, so an R_i-invariant A has A^j_{R_i y} = A^j_y.
(R_i y)_j = y_j for i ≠ j, hence R_i(y) ∈ S_j(A).

subproblems.title: Steiner symmetrization does not increase the diameter
subproblems.statement: Let d ∈ ℕ, j ∈ Fin d and let A ⊆ ℝ^d = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) be compact. With y[j↦t] := y with its j-th coordinate replaced by t (Lean: WithLp.toLp 2 (Function.update y.ofLp j t)), A^j_y := {t ∈ ℝ : y[j↦t] ∈ A}, λ(y) := (L¹(A^j_y)).toReal and S_j(A) := {y ∈ ℝ^d : A^j_y ≠ ∅ and |y_j| ≤ λ(y)/2}, the extended diameters satisfy ediam S_j(A) ≤ ediam A.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (d : ℕ) (j : Fin d) (A : Set (Euclid d)), IsCompact A → ediam {y : Euclid d | {t : ℝ | WithLp.toLp 2 (Function.update y.ofLp j t) ∈ A}.Nonempty ∧ |y j| ≤ (volume {t : ℝ | WithLp.toLp 2 (Function.update y.ofLp j t) ∈ A}).toReal / 2} ≤ ediam A
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent step 1e (Simon, Ch. 1, proof of 2.10, book/chapter-01.txt lines 523–525: S_j(A) has diameter not larger than that of A). Notation: y[j↦t] = WithLp.toLp 2 (Function.update y.ofLp j t), y_j = y j; with ξ = y[j↦0], A^j_y is the parent's A_ξ and λ(y) = λ(ξ), so S_j(A) is the parent's set.
1. Slices are compact and uniformly bounded. A is bounded, so A ⊆ closedBall(0, R) for some R (IsBounded.subset_closedBall). For y ∈ ℝ^d and t ∈ A^j_y: |t| = |(y[j↦t])_j| ≤ ‖y[j↦t]‖ ≤ R (PiLp.norm_apply_le), so A^j_y ⊆ [−R, R]. A^j_y is the preimage of the closed set A under the continuous map t ↦ y[j↦t] (PiLp.continuous_toLp composed with Continuous.update), hence closed; being closed and bounded in ℝ, it is compact.
2. Length versus spread. Let P ⊆ ℝ be compact and nonempty, a := inf P, b := sup P. Then a, b ∈ P (IsCompact.sInf_mem, IsCompact.sSup_mem), a ≤ b and P ⊆ [a, b] (csInf_le, le_csSup), so L¹(P) ≤ L¹([a, b]) = ofReal(b − a) (Real.volume_Icc), hence (L¹(P)).toReal ≤ b − a.
3. Replacing one coordinate. For x, y ∈ ℝ^d and a, b ∈ ℝ: |x[j↦a] − y[j↦b]|² = |x − y|² − (x_j − y_j)² + (a − b)². Indeed |u − v|² = Σ_i (u_i − v_i)² (EuclideanSpace.dist_sq_eq); after splitting off the index j (Finset.sum_erase_add), the terms with i ≠ j coincide for (x, y) and (x[j↦a], y[j↦b]), while the j-th terms are (x_j − y_j)² and (a − b)².
4. Two-point estimate. If x[j↦a] ∈ A, y[j↦b] ∈ A and |x_j − y_j| ≤ |a − b|, then (x_j − y_j)² ≤ (a − b)², so by step 3 |x − y|² ≤ |x[j↦a] − y[j↦b]|², and since distances are nonnegative, |x − y| ≤ |x[j↦a] − y[j↦b]|. Hence edist(x, y) = ofReal|x − y| ≤ edist(x[j↦a], y[j↦b]) ≤ ediam A (edist_dist, ENNReal.ofReal_le_ofReal, edist_le_ediam_of_mem).
5. Let x, y ∈ S_j(A). Then P := A^j_x and Q := A^j_y are nonempty and compact (step 1). Put a_x := inf P, b_x := sup P, a_y := inf Q, b_y := sup Q. By step 2 the four points x[j↦a_x], x[j↦b_x], y[j↦a_y], y[j↦b_y] lie in A, and λ(x) ≤ b_x − a_x, λ(y) ≤ b_y − a_y. Since |x_j| ≤ λ(x)/2 and |y_j| ≤ λ(y)/2: |x_j − y_j| ≤ |x_j| + |y_j| ≤ (λ(x) + λ(y))/2 ≤ ((b_x − a_x) + (b_y − a_y))/2 = ((b_y − a_x) + (b_x − a_y))/2.
6. If b_x − a_y ≤ b_y − a_x, step 5 gives |x_j − y_j| ≤ b_y − a_x; in particular b_y − a_x ≥ 0, so b_y − a_x = |a_x − b_y|, and step 4 with (a, b) = (a_x, b_y) gives edist(x, y) ≤ ediam A. If b_y − a_x ≤ b_x − a_y, then likewise |x_j − y_j| ≤ b_x − a_y = |b_x − a_y|, and step 4 with (a, b) = (b_x, a_y) gives edist(x, y) ≤ ediam A.
7. As edist(x, y) ≤ ediam A for all x, y ∈ S_j(A), ediam S_j(A) ≤ ediam A (ediam_le). ∎
proof_key_steps: Slices A^j_y are compact subsets of [−R, R].
For a nonempty compact P ⊆ ℝ: inf P, sup P ∈ P and (L¹ P).toReal ≤ sup P − inf P.
|x[j↦a] − y[j↦b]|² = |x − y|² − (x_j − y_j)² + (a − b)².
|x_j − y_j| ≤ (λ(x)+λ(y))/2 ≤ max(b_y − a_x, b_x − a_y), realised by a pair of points of A whose distance is ≥ |x − y|.
Hence edist(x, y) ≤ ediam A for all x, y ∈ S_j(A).

subproblems.title: Upper semicontinuity of the slice length (Simon's note to 2.10)
subproblems.statement: Let d ∈ ℕ, j ∈ Fin d and let A ⊆ ℝ^d = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) be compact. For y ∈ ℝ^d let λ(y) := (L¹({t ∈ ℝ : y[j↦t] ∈ A})).toReal, where y[j↦t] is y with its j-th coordinate replaced by t (Lean: WithLp.toLp 2 (Function.update y.ofLp j t)) and L¹ is Lebesgue measure on ℝ. Then λ : ℝ^d → ℝ is upper semicontinuous: for every x ∈ ℝ^d and every real r > λ(x) there is a neighbourhood N of x with λ(y) < r for all y ∈ N.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (d : ℕ) (j : Fin d) (A : Set (Euclid d)), IsCompact A → UpperSemicontinuous (fun y : Euclid d => (volume {t : ℝ | WithLp.toLp 2 (Function.update y.ofLp j t) ∈ A}).toReal)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon's note after the proof of 2.10 (Ch. 1, book/chapter-01.txt lines 537–545) and parent step 1c (choose an open U ⊇ A_ξ with L¹(U) ≤ λ(ξ) + ε and use the compactness of A). The parent's subsequence argument is written here as the closedness of a compact projection. Notation: A^j_y := {t ∈ ℝ : y[j↦t] ∈ A}, y[j↦t] = WithLp.toLp 2 (Function.update y.ofLp j t), λ(y) = (L¹(A^j_y)).toReal. In Mathlib, UpperSemicontinuous λ means: for all x and r with λ(x) < r, eventually for y in 𝓝 x, λ(y) < r.
1. Slices have finite measure. A ⊆ closedBall(0, R) for some R; for t ∈ A^j_y, |t| ≤ ‖y[j↦t]‖ ≤ R (PiLp.norm_apply_le), so A^j_y ⊆ [−R, R] and L¹(A^j_y) ≤ L¹([−R, R]) < ∞. Hence ofReal(λ(y)) = L¹(A^j_y) for every y (ENNReal.ofReal_toReal).
2. Fix x ∈ ℝ^d and r > λ(x). Then L¹(A^j_x) = ofReal(λ(x)) < ofReal(r) (ENNReal.ofReal_lt_ofReal_iff_of_nonneg). By outer regularity of Lebesgue measure on ℝ there is an open set U ⊇ A^j_x with L¹(U) < ofReal(r) (Set.exists_isOpen_lt_of_lt).
3. Let O := {z ∈ ℝ^d : z_j ∈ U}, open as the preimage of U under the continuous coordinate map z ↦ z_j, and C := A ∖ O, compact as a closed subset of the compact set A (IsCompact.diff). Let π(z) := z[j↦0]; π is continuous, so π(C) is compact and hence closed.
4. Same projection. If π(z) = π(y), then z = y[j↦z_j]: for i ≠ j, z_i = (π z)_i = (π y)_i = y_i, and the j-th coordinates of both sides equal z_j. Moreover π(y[j↦t]) = π(y) for all t.
5. π(x) ∉ π(C). Otherwise π(z) = π(x) for some z ∈ C ⊆ A; by step 4, x[j↦z_j] = z ∈ A, so z_j ∈ A^j_x ⊆ U, i.e. z ∈ O, contradicting z ∈ C = A ∖ O.
6. Hence N := π⁻¹(ℝ^d ∖ π(C)) is open (continuity of π) and contains x, so it is a neighbourhood of x. For y ∈ N we have A^j_y ⊆ U: if t ∈ A^j_y but t ∉ U, then z := y[j↦t] ∈ A with z_j = t ∉ U, so z ∈ C, and π(z) = π(y) by step 4, so π(y) ∈ π(C), contradicting y ∈ N.
7. For y ∈ N: L¹(A^j_y) ≤ L¹(U) < ofReal(r), hence λ(y) = (L¹(A^j_y)).toReal < r (ENNReal.toReal_lt_of_lt_ofReal). Thus λ(y) < r on the neighbourhood N of x; since x and r were arbitrary, λ is upper semicontinuous. ∎
proof_key_steps: Slices lie in [−R, R], so ofReal(λ y) = L¹(A^j_y) < ∞.
Outer regularity gives an open U ⊇ A^j_x with L¹(U) < ofReal r.
C := A ∖ {z : z_j ∈ U} is compact; its projection π(C), π(z) = z[j↦0], is closed and does not contain π(x).
On the neighbourhood π⁻¹(π(C)ᶜ) of x every slice lies in U, so λ < r there.

subproblems.title: Steiner symmetrization of a compact set is compact
subproblems.statement: Let d ∈ ℕ, j ∈ Fin d and let A ⊆ ℝ^d = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) be compact. Let A^j_y := {t ∈ ℝ : y[j↦t] ∈ A}, where y[j↦t] is y with its j-th coordinate replaced by t (Lean: WithLp.toLp 2 (Function.update y.ofLp j t)), and λ(y) := (L¹(A^j_y)).toReal. If λ : ℝ^d → ℝ is upper semicontinuous, then the Steiner symmetrization S_j(A) := {y ∈ ℝ^d : A^j_y ≠ ∅ and |y_j| ≤ λ(y)/2} is compact.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (d : ℕ) (j : Fin d) (A : Set (Euclid d)), IsCompact A → UpperSemicontinuous (fun y : Euclid d => (volume {t : ℝ | WithLp.toLp 2 (Function.update y.ofLp j t) ∈ A}).toReal) → IsCompact {y : Euclid d | {t : ℝ | WithLp.toLp 2 (Function.update y.ofLp j t) ∈ A}.Nonempty ∧ |y j| ≤ (volume {t : ℝ | WithLp.toLp 2 (Function.update y.ofLp j t) ∈ A}).toReal / 2}
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent step 1c and Simon's note after 2.10 (Ch. 1, book/chapter-01.txt lines 523–524 and 537–545) (S_j(A) is compact because the slice length is upper semicontinuous); the upper semicontinuity is the hypothesis. Notation: A^j_y := {t ∈ ℝ : y[j↦t] ∈ A}, y[j↦t] = WithLp.toLp 2 (Function.update y.ofLp j t), λ(y) = (L¹(A^j_y)).toReal, π(z) := z[j↦0].
1. π is continuous; π(y[j↦t]) = π(y) for all t; and π(z) = π(y) implies z = y[j↦z_j] (the coordinates with index i ≠ j agree, and both j-th coordinates equal z_j).
2. N := {y : A^j_y ≠ ∅} equals π⁻¹(π(A)). If t ∈ A^j_y, then y[j↦t] ∈ A and π(y[j↦t]) = π(y), so π(y) ∈ π(A). Conversely, if π(z) = π(y) with z ∈ A, then y[j↦z_j] = z ∈ A by step 1, so z_j ∈ A^j_y. Since π(A) is compact (continuous image of a compact set), it is closed, so N is closed.
3. M := {y : |y_j| ≤ λ(y)/2} is closed. The function f(y) := λ(y) + (−2|y_j|) is upper semicontinuous as the sum of the upper semicontinuous λ and a continuous function (UpperSemicontinuous.add, Continuous.upperSemicontinuous). Superlevel sets of upper semicontinuous functions are closed (UpperSemicontinuous.isClosed_preimage: f⁻¹([0, ∞)) is closed), and |y_j| ≤ λ(y)/2 ⟺ 0 ≤ f(y), so M = f⁻¹([0, ∞)) is closed.
4. S_j(A) = N ∩ M (its defining condition is the conjunction of the two conditions; Set.ofPred_and), hence S_j(A) is closed.
5. S_j(A) is bounded. A ⊆ closedBall(0, R) for some R. Let y ∈ S_j(A) and choose t ∈ A^j_y; then y[j↦t] ∈ A, so ‖y[j↦t]‖ ≤ R, and in particular R ≥ 0. Every s ∈ A^j_y satisfies |s| ≤ ‖y[j↦s]‖ ≤ R (PiLp.norm_apply_le), so A^j_y ⊆ [−R, R], L¹(A^j_y) ≤ ofReal(2R) and λ(y) ≤ 2R; thus |y_j| ≤ λ(y)/2 ≤ R, and |t| ≤ R. The vector y − y[j↦t] has j-th coordinate y_j − t and all other coordinates 0, so ‖y − y[j↦t]‖ = |y_j − t| (EuclideanSpace.norm_eq). Hence ‖y‖ ≤ ‖y[j↦t]‖ + ‖y − y[j↦t]‖ ≤ R + |y_j| + |t| ≤ 3R, i.e. S_j(A) ⊆ closedBall(0, 3R).
6. ℝ^d is a proper metric space, so the closed and bounded set S_j(A) is compact (isCompact_of_isClosed_isBounded). ∎
proof_key_steps: {y : A^j_y ≠ ∅} = π⁻¹(π(A)) with π(z) = z[j↦0] is closed.
{y : |y_j| ≤ λ(y)/2} is the superlevel set {λ − 2|y_j| ≥ 0} of an upper semicontinuous function, hence closed.
Every y ∈ S_j(A) satisfies ‖y‖ ≤ 3R.
Closed and bounded in ℝ^d implies compact.

subproblems.title: Cavalieri's principle along a coordinate direction
subproblems.statement: Let d ∈ ℕ, j ∈ Fin d, and let S, A ⊆ ℝ^d = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) be measurable sets. For y ∈ ℝ^d and t ∈ ℝ let y[j↦t] be y with its j-th coordinate replaced by t (Lean: WithLp.toLp 2 (Function.update y.ofLp j t)). Suppose that for every y ∈ ℝ^d the line slices through y in direction e_j have equal one-dimensional Lebesgue measure: L¹({t ∈ ℝ : y[j↦t] ∈ S}) = L¹({t ∈ ℝ : y[j↦t] ∈ A}). Then L^d(S) = L^d(A). Here L^d is the volume (Lebesgue measure) of EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) and L¹ is the volume of ℝ.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (d : ℕ) (j : Fin d) (S A : Set (Euclid d)), MeasurableSet S → MeasurableSet A → (∀ y : Euclid d, volume {t : ℝ | WithLp.toLp 2 (Function.update y.ofLp j t) ∈ S} = volume {t : ℝ | WithLp.toLp 2 (Function.update y.ofLp j t) ∈ A}) → volume S = volume A
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent step 1d (Simon Ch. 1, proof of 2.10, book/chapter-01.txt lines 523–525: the Steiner symmetral has, 'by Fubini', the same Lebesgue measure as A): the measure-preserving identification of ℝ^d with ℝ × ℝ^{d−1} that splits off the j-th coordinate, followed by Tonelli. The parent's computation of the slices of S_j(A) is not part of this statement: equality of the slice measures through every base point is the hypothesis. Notation: y[j↦t] := WithLp.toLp 2 (Function.update y.ofLp j t); for B ⊆ ℝ^d and y ∈ ℝ^d, B^j_y := {t ∈ ℝ : y[j↦t] ∈ B}.
1. Since j ∈ Fin d, Fin d is nonempty, so d ≠ 0. (For d = 0 the element j : Fin 0 does not exist, and Fin.elim0 j closes the goal.) Write d = n + 1.
2. Product coordinates. Let e := MeasurableEquiv.piFinSuccAbove (fun _ => ℝ) j : (Fin (n+1) → ℝ) ≃ᵐ ℝ × (Fin n → ℝ). By volume_preserving_piFinSuccAbove, e is measure preserving from volume to volume. On ℝ × (Fin n → ℝ), volume is the product measure L¹ ⊗ L^n = volume.prod volume, and both factors are σ-finite. The inverse is e.symm (t, z) = Fin.insertNth j t z. Put φ(t, z) := WithLp.toLp 2 (e.symm (t, z)) = WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.insertNth j t z) ∈ ℝ^d. The map e.symm is measure preserving (MeasurePreserving.symm), and so is WithLp.toLp 2 : (Fin (n+1) → ℝ) → ℝ^d (PiLp.volume_preserving_toLp). Hence the composite φ is measure preserving from L¹ ⊗ L^n to L^d (MeasurePreserving.comp), and in particular φ is measurable.
3. Fibres of φ are coordinate slices. Fix z ∈ Fin n → ℝ and set y_z := φ(0, z). Then y_z.ofLp = Fin.insertNth j 0 z (WithLp.ofLp_toLp). For t ∈ ℝ, Fin.update_insertNth gives Function.update (Fin.insertNth j 0 z) j t = Fin.insertNth j t z, so y_z[j↦t] = φ(t, z). Hence for every B ⊆ ℝ^d: {t ∈ ℝ : φ(t, z) ∈ B} = B^j_{y_z}.
4. Equal fibre measures. Apply the hypothesis at y = y_z and use step 3 with B = S and with B = A: L¹({t : φ(t, z) ∈ S}) = L¹(S^j_{y_z}) = L¹(A^j_{y_z}) = L¹({t : φ(t, z) ∈ A}). This holds for every z ∈ Fin n → ℝ.
5. Tonelli and measure preservation. S is measurable and φ is measurable, so φ⁻¹(S) ⊆ ℝ × (Fin n → ℝ) is measurable. Measure.prod_apply_symm then gives (L¹ ⊗ L^n)(φ⁻¹ S) = ∫⁻ z, L¹({t : (t, z) ∈ φ⁻¹ S}) dz = ∫⁻ z, L¹({t : φ(t, z) ∈ S}) dz. Since φ is measure preserving and S is measurable (hence null-measurable), MeasurePreserving.measure_preimage gives L^d(S) = (L¹ ⊗ L^n)(φ⁻¹ S). The same two facts hold with A in place of S, because A is measurable.
6. Conclusion. L^d(S) = (L¹ ⊗ L^n)(φ⁻¹ S) = ∫⁻ z, L¹({t : φ(t, z) ∈ S}) dz = ∫⁻ z, L¹({t : φ(t, z) ∈ A}) dz = (L¹ ⊗ L^n)(φ⁻¹ A) = L^d(A). The middle equality is lintegral_congr applied with step 4; the other equalities are step 5. ∎
proof_key_steps: d = n + 1 (Fin.elim0 handles d = 0). φ(t, z) := WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.insertNth j t z) is measure preserving from L¹ ⊗ L^n to L^d (volume_preserving_piFinSuccAbove, MeasurePreserving.symm, PiLp.volume_preserving_toLp, MeasurePreserving.comp).
Fin.update_insertNth gives φ(0, z)[j↦t] = φ(t, z), so every fibre {t : φ(t, z) ∈ B} equals the slice B^j_{φ(0, z)}.
The hypothesis at y = φ(0, z) gives L¹({t : φ(t, z) ∈ S}) = L¹({t : φ(t, z) ∈ A}) for every z.
Measure.prod_apply_symm on the measurable sets φ⁻¹S and φ⁻¹A, lintegral_congr and MeasurePreserving.measure_preimage give L^d(S) = L^d(A).

subproblems.title: Line slices of the Steiner symmetral have the length of the slices of A
subproblems.statement: Let d ∈ ℕ, j ∈ Fin d and let A ⊆ ℝ^d = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) be compact. For x ∈ ℝ^d and s ∈ ℝ let x[j↦s] be x with its j-th coordinate replaced by s (Lean: WithLp.toLp 2 (Function.update x.ofLp j s)). Let A^j_x := {s ∈ ℝ : x[j↦s] ∈ A} and S_j(A) := {x ∈ ℝ^d : A^j_x ≠ ∅ and |x_j| ≤ (L¹(A^j_x)).toReal/2}. Then for every y ∈ ℝ^d, L¹({t ∈ ℝ : y[j↦t] ∈ S_j(A)}) = L¹(A^j_y), where L¹ is the volume (Lebesgue measure) of ℝ.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (d : ℕ) (j : Fin d) (A : Set (Euclid d)), IsCompact A → ∀ y : Euclid d, volume {t : ℝ | WithLp.toLp 2 (Function.update y.ofLp j t) ∈ {x : Euclid d | {s : ℝ | WithLp.toLp 2 (Function.update x.ofLp j s) ∈ A}.Nonempty ∧ |x j| ≤ (volume {s : ℝ | WithLp.toLp 2 (Function.update x.ofLp j s) ∈ A}).toReal / 2}} = volume {t : ℝ | WithLp.toLp 2 (Function.update y.ofLp j t) ∈ A}
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent step 1d, the slice computation 'S_j(A)_ξ = [−λ(ξ)/2, λ(ξ)/2] has length λ(ξ) for ξ ∈ π_j(A) and is empty otherwise', written for the line through an arbitrary point y ∈ ℝ^d (Simon Ch. 1, proof of 2.10, book/chapter-01.txt lines 512–522: S_j(A) meets each line ℓ_j(ξ) that meets A in the closed segment {|t| ≤ ½ L¹(A ∩ ℓ_j(ξ))}). Notation: x[j↦s] := WithLp.toLp 2 (Function.update x.ofLp j s), A^j_x := {s ∈ ℝ : x[j↦s] ∈ A}, x_j := x.ofLp j. Fix y ∈ ℝ^d and put B := A^j_y, ℓ := (L¹(B)).toReal ≥ 0 and F := {t ∈ ℝ : y[j↦t] ∈ S_j(A)}. We must show L¹(F) = L¹(B).
1. Coordinate identities. For t ∈ ℝ, (y[j↦t]).ofLp = Function.update y.ofLp j t (WithLp.ofLp_toLp), so (y[j↦t])_j = Function.update y.ofLp j t j = t (Function.update_self). For t, s ∈ ℝ, Function.update (Function.update y.ofLp j t) j s = Function.update y.ofLp j s (Function.update_idem), so (y[j↦t])[j↦s] = y[j↦s]. Consequently A^j_{y[j↦t]} = {s : y[j↦s] ∈ A} = B for every t ∈ ℝ.
2. Description of F. By the definition of S_j(A), t ∈ F iff A^j_{y[j↦t]} ≠ ∅ and |(y[j↦t])_j| ≤ (L¹(A^j_{y[j↦t]})).toReal/2. By step 1 this condition reads: B ≠ ∅ and |t| ≤ ℓ/2. So F = {t ∈ ℝ : B ≠ ∅ ∧ |t| ≤ ℓ/2}.
3. L¹(B) < ∞. The coordinate map π : ℝ^d → ℝ, π(x) := x_j, is continuous, so π(A) is compact (IsCompact.image) and L¹(π(A)) < ∞ (IsCompact.measure_lt_top). If t ∈ B, then x := y[j↦t] ∈ A and π(x) = t by step 1. Thus B ⊆ π(A), and L¹(B) < ∞ by measure_lt_top_of_subset.
4. Case B = ∅. No t satisfies the condition of step 2, so F = ∅ and L¹(F) = 0 = L¹(∅) = L¹(B).
5. Case B ≠ ∅. Then F = {t : |t| ≤ ℓ/2} = [−ℓ/2, ℓ/2] (abs_le). By Real.volume_Icc, L¹(F) = ofReal(ℓ/2 − (−ℓ/2)) = ofReal(ℓ) = ofReal((L¹(B)).toReal). This equals L¹(B) by ENNReal.ofReal_toReal, which applies because L¹(B) ≠ ∞ by step 3. (When ℓ = 0, F = {0} and both sides are 0.)
6. In both cases L¹({t : y[j↦t] ∈ S_j(A)}) = L¹(F) = L¹(B) = L¹(A^j_y). Since y ∈ ℝ^d was arbitrary, the claim holds for every y. ∎
proof_key_steps: (y[j↦t])_j = t and (y[j↦t])[j↦s] = y[j↦s] (WithLp.ofLp_toLp, Function.update_self, Function.update_idem), so A^j_{y[j↦t]} = A^j_y =: B for every t.
Hence {t : y[j↦t] ∈ S_j(A)} = {t : B ≠ ∅ ∧ |t| ≤ (L¹ B).toReal / 2}.
B is contained in the compact image π_j(A), so L¹(B) < ∞.
If B = ∅ both measures are 0. Otherwise the set is Icc (−ℓ/2) (ℓ/2), whose measure is ofReal ℓ = L¹(B) (Real.volume_Icc, ENNReal.ofReal_toReal).

subproblems.title: Isodiametric bound for centrally symmetric sets
subproblems.statement: For every d ∈ ℕ and every set K ⊆ ℝ^d = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) such that −x ∈ K whenever x ∈ K (no measurability or boundedness assumed): L^d(K) ≤ ω_d·(ediam K/2)^d in [0, ∞]. Here L^d = volume, ω_d = unitBallVolume d = L^d(ball(0, 1)), and ediam is the extended diameter.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (d : ℕ) (K : Set (Euclid d)), (∀ x ∈ K, -x ∈ K) → volume K ≤ unitBallVolume d * (ediam K / 2) ^ d
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: final step of Simon's proof of 2.10 (Ch. 1, book/chapter-01.txt lines 530–536) / parent step 1g (the symmetrized set lies in the closed ball of radius ½ diam about 0, whence the bound). No measurability, compactness or boundedness of K is assumed.
1. ω_d ∈ (0, ∞): the open unit ball is a nonempty open set, so its volume is positive (Metric.measure_ball_pos for the additive Haar measure volume); it is bounded, so its volume is finite (measure_ball_lt_top).
2. Case ediam K = ∞. Then d ≥ 1: for d = 0, ℝ⁰ has exactly one point, so K is subsingleton and ediam K = 0 (ediam_subsingleton). For d ≥ 1, (∞/2)^d = ∞ (ENNReal.top_div_of_ne_top, ENNReal.top_pow) and ω_d·∞ = ∞ (ENNReal.mul_top, ω_d ≠ 0), so the inequality holds trivially.
3. Case ediam K < ∞. Then K is bounded (isBounded_iff_ediam_ne_top). For x ∈ K also −x ∈ K, so 2‖x‖ = ‖x − (−x)‖ = dist(x, −x) ≤ diam K (dist_le_diam_of_mem). Hence K ⊆ closedBall(0, r) with r := diam K/2 ≥ 0.
4. L^d(closedBall(0, r)) = ofReal(r^d)·ω_d. By Measure.addHaar_closedBall for the additive Haar measure volume, L^d(closedBall(0, r)) = ofReal(r^{finrank})·L^d(ball(0, 1)), and finrank ℝ (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)) = d (finrank_euclideanSpace_fin). This holds for every d, including 0.
5. ofReal(r^d) = ofReal(r)^d = (ofReal(diam K)/2)^d = (ediam K/2)^d. This uses r ≥ 0 (ENNReal.ofReal_pow), ofReal(a/2) = ofReal(a)/2 (ENNReal.ofReal_div_of_pos), and ofReal(diam K) = ofReal((ediam K).toReal) = ediam K because ediam K ≠ ∞ (ENNReal.ofReal_toReal).
6. By monotonicity of measure, L^d(K) ≤ L^d(closedBall(0, r)) = ω_d·(ediam K/2)^d. ∎
proof_key_steps: ω_d = unitBallVolume d is positive and finite.
ediam K = ∞ forces d ≥ 1 and an infinite right-hand side.
Central symmetry gives K ⊆ closedBall(0, diam K/2).
L^d(closedBall(0, r)) = ofReal(r^d)·ω_d and ofReal(diam K/2)^d = (ediam K/2)^d.

subproblems.title: Iterated Steiner symmetrization gives a centrally symmetric compact replacement
subproblems.statement: For every d ∈ ℕ and every compact A ⊆ ℝ^d = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) there is a compact K ⊆ ℝ^d with L^d(K) = L^d(A) (L^d = volume), ediam K ≤ ediam A, and −x ∈ K for every x ∈ K.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (d : ℕ) (A : Set (Euclid d)), IsCompact A → ∃ K : Set (Euclid d), IsCompact K ∧ volume K = volume A ∧ ediam K ≤ ediam A ∧ ∀ x ∈ K, -x ∈ K
proof_key_steps: Volume preservation for compact B: S_i(B) is compact by (U) and (C), hence measurable; the slice equality (L) and the coordinate Cavalieri principle (F) give L^d(S_i(B)) = L^d(B).
Finset induction over the processed coordinates, replacing K by S_i(K).
Each step preserves compactness, Lebesgue measure and the ediam bound (D), keeps the old reflection symmetries and adds R_i-symmetry (R).
After all coordinates, K is invariant under every R_i.
Flipping the coordinates of x ∈ K one at a time gives −x ∈ K.

subproblems.title: Isodiametric inequality (Simon 2.10)
subproblems.statement: Isodiametric inequality: for every d ∈ ℕ and every set A ⊆ ℝ^d = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) (not necessarily measurable or bounded), L^d(A) ≤ ω_d·(ediam A/2)^d in [0, ∞]. Here L^d = volume, ω_d = unitBallVolume d = L^d(ball(0, 1)), and ediam is the extended diameter.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (d : ℕ) (A : Set (Euclid d)), volume A ≤ unitBallVolume d * (ediam A / 2) ^ d
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 1, Theorem 2.10 and its proof (book/chapter-01.txt lines 502–536) / parent steps 1a (reduction to compact sets) and 1g (conclusion).
1. ω_d ≠ 0: the open unit ball is nonempty and open, so its volume is positive (Metric.measure_ball_pos).
2. Case ediam A = ∞. Then d ≥ 1: for d = 0 every subset of the one-point space ℝ⁰ is subsingleton and has ediam 0 (ediam_subsingleton). Hence (ediam A/2)^d = (∞/2)^d = ∞ (ENNReal.top_div_of_ne_top, ENNReal.top_pow), the right-hand side is ω_d·∞ = ∞ (ENNReal.mul_top, using ω_d ≠ 0), and the inequality holds.
3. Case ediam A < ∞ (reduction 1a). A is bounded (isBounded_iff_ediam_ne_top), so its closure Ā is compact (Bornology.IsBounded.isCompact_closure; ℝ^d is proper). Moreover ediam Ā = ediam A (Metric.ediam_closure) and L^d(A) ≤ L^d(Ā) (monotonicity, A ⊆ Ā).
4. By the sibling Submission.dmcbr_ci_iso_exists_symmetric_replacement applied to the compact set Ā, there is a compact K with L^d(K) = L^d(Ā), ediam K ≤ ediam Ā = ediam A, and −x ∈ K for all x ∈ K.
5. By the sibling Submission.cbr_ci_iso_volume_le_of_neg_mem, L^d(K) ≤ ω_d·(ediam K/2)^d. Since t ↦ ω_d·(t/2)^d is monotone on [0, ∞] and ediam K ≤ ediam A, ω_d·(ediam K/2)^d ≤ ω_d·(ediam A/2)^d (gcongr).
6. Hence L^d(A) ≤ L^d(Ā) = L^d(K) ≤ ω_d·(ediam A/2)^d. ∎
proof_key_steps: Unbounded A: d ≥ 1 and the right-hand side is ∞.
Bounded A: pass to the compact closure, which has the same ediam and at least the same measure.
Replace the closure by a centrally symmetric compact set of equal measure and no larger ediam (symmetric_replacement).
Apply the centrally symmetric bound (symmetric_bound) and monotonicity in ediam.

subproblems.title: Lebesgue measure is at most (ω_d/2^d)·μH[d] on ℝ^d (completion of Simon 2.9)
subproblems.statement: For every d ∈ ℕ, the Lebesgue measure L^d = volume on ℝ^d = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) is dominated by (ω_d/2^d)·μH[d]: L^d(s) ≤ (ω_d/2^d)·μH[d](s) for every set s ⊆ ℝ^d (as measures, L^d ≤ (ω_d/2^d)•μH[d]). Here ω_d = unitBallVolume d = L^d(ball(0, 1)), and μH[d] is Mathlib's d-dimensional Hausdorff measure (weight diam^d, no normalising constant).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (d : ℕ), (volume : Measure (Euclid d)) ≤ (unitBallVolume d / 2 ^ d) • (μH[(d : ℝ)] : Measure (Euclid d))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 1, 'Completion of the proof of 2.9' (book/chapter-01.txt lines 547–559) / parent step 2, translated to Mathlib's normalisation of μH[d] (weight ediam^d, no normalising constant).
1. Let c := ω_d/2^d. Then c ≠ 0, since ω_d ≠ 0 (Metric.measure_ball_pos) and 2^d ≠ ∞ (ENNReal.div_ne_zero). Also c ≠ ∞, since ω_d < ∞ (measure_ball_lt_top) and 2^d ≠ 0 (ENNReal.div_ne_top).
2. For every set s ⊆ ℝ^d, the sibling isodiametric inequality Submission.dmcbr_ci_iso_volume_le_ediam_pow gives L^d(s) ≤ ω_d·(ediam s/2)^d = ω_d·ediam(s)^d·(2^d)⁻¹ = c·ediam(s)^d. The ENNReal arithmetic uses a/2 = a·2⁻¹ (div_eq_mul_inv), mul_pow, ENNReal.inv_pow and commutativity. Multiplying by c⁻¹: c⁻¹·L^d(s) ≤ c⁻¹·c·ediam(s)^d = ediam(s)^d (ENNReal.inv_mul_cancel, valid as c ∉ {0, ∞}).
3. Let ν := c⁻¹•L^d, a measure. By step 2, ν(s) ≤ ediam(s)^d = ediam(s)^(d : ℝ) for every set s (ENNReal.rpow_natCast). Hence ν ≤ μH[d]. Indeed, for any δ > 0 and any countable cover (C_k) of a set B by sets with ediam C_k ≤ δ, ν(B) ≤ Σ_k ν(C_k) ≤ Σ_k ediam(C_k)^d; taking the infimum over such covers and the supremum over δ > 0 gives ν(B) ≤ μH[d](B). In Mathlib this is exactly Measure.le_hausdorffMeasure (d : ℝ) ν 1 one_pos: its hypothesis is required only for sets of ediam ≤ 1, and step 2 gives it for all sets.
4. For every set s: L^d(s) = c·(c⁻¹·L^d(s)) = c·ν(s) ≤ c·μH[d](s) (ENNReal.mul_inv_cancel and monotonicity of multiplication). By the setwise characterisation of ≤ for measures (Measure.le_iff'), L^d ≤ c•μH[d]. ∎
proof_key_steps: c = ω_d/2^d is positive and finite.
The isodiametric inequality rewritten: L^d(s) ≤ c·ediam(s)^d, i.e. c⁻¹L^d(s) ≤ ediam(s)^d for all s.
Measure.le_hausdorffMeasure gives c⁻¹•L^d ≤ μH[d].
Multiplying back by c gives L^d ≤ c•μH[d] setwise.
